correctness.rationale: The quantile identity gives \(\lambda_2=2\operatorname{Cov}(Q(U),U)\). Conditioning on the atom-bin index \(J\) replaces \(U\) by its conditional midpoint \(m_J\), so Cauchy--Schwarz yields \(\lambda_2^2\le4\sigma^2\operatorname{Var}(m_J)\). Total variance of a uniform variable gives \(\operatorname{Var}(m_J)=(1-\sum_i p_i^3)/12\). Equality in Cauchy--Schwarz is exactly the stated affine-midpoint geometry, and strict convexity of \(t^3\) gives the support-count corollary. The derivation was reconstructed directly from RESULT.md; the numerical stress test is not needed for the proof.
risks: The theorem is finite-atomic only; no countably infinite-support extension is claimed.

value.rationale: This is a sharp structural refinement of a standard scale inequality for every prescribed finite mass vector, with complete equality geometry and a sharp support-size envelope. It quantifies exactly how atomicity improves the universal Gini/variance constant.

final_claim: For every nondegenerate finitely supported real law with positive atom masses \(p_i\), the second L-moment obeys \(\lambda_2^2\le \sigma^2(1-\sum_i p_i^3)/3\), sharply for each fixed mass vector, with equality exactly at affine quantile-bin midpoints; consequently \(G/\sigma\le 2\sqrt{(1-N^{-2})/3}\) for exactly \(N\) atoms, with equality only for a uniform equally spaced lattice.
limitations: Finite positive atom masses and nonzero variance only.
